pages.title: Comala Document Management Cloud FDA Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance Statement

content.text: If you are using Confluence and Comala Document Control Cloud within an FDA-regulated environment, then you might need to setup Confluence following the FDA CFR 21 part 11 regulation -
This article provides an overview of how companies are using these tools to achieve compliance and draws directly from our customers' real-life experiences.

This article assumes that Confluence Cloud is set up as a 'closed system’. 'Closed system’ is a regulatory term and refers to a situation where you control access to the system. This would be the typical scenario within the corporate world and hence was used here as a key assumption.
For our purposes, the CFR 21 part 11 covers two areas:

Electronic Records: This area relates to the data stored and managed within the system: your Confluence pages. It imposes requirements on the system to ensure that electronic data can be used instead of paper documents (Subpart B)

Electronic Signatures: This area relates to how people can electronically sign documents and forms (i.e. Confluence pages), with the purpose that these electronic signatures substitute paper signatures (also known as 'wet signatures') (Subpart C)
This article covers both these areas and focuses on how Comala Document Management Cloud contributes to achieving compliance.
For an organization to be in compliance, the right tools must be paired with the appropriate quality processes. We outline these in the compliance table below.

A word of caution: the content and information you keep in Confluence and how it is used within your quality management system will impact your compliance strategy. We highly recommend that you seek specific advice from a regulatory expert regarding the optimal setup for your organization.

Appfire does not claim compliance or certification of any of our tools, as it is impossible for any vendor to offer a compliant system. In addition to taking advantage of technical elements, compliant systems must implement procedural and administrative controls.
Need help setting up Confluence and Comala Document Management Cloud for controlled documents?
1. The Toolset Required to set up a Compliant Document Management System in Confluence
The following table shows what tools are needed to create a compliant configuration:
The platform for creating, storing, and using electronic records.
An Appfire Comala app for Confluence provides a way to enforce an approval process for documents. Comala Document Control Cloud provides a preset

that implements a typical document approval process. The preset workflow can be modified using a Workflow Builder to reflect your documented approval process. Built-in electronic signatures and an audit log support this approval process.

Comala Document Management adds review and approval workflows to Confluence Cloud. Teams can assign reviewers, set deadlines, and track a document's lifecycle. Integrated reporting tools provide oversight of all status changes and approvals within a space.

A workflow defines the stages a document moves through, such as Draft, In Review, and Approved. You can create workflows with any number of stages and apply them to individual pages or entire spaces. A single workflow can be reused across multiple pages and spaces.
is the current stage of a document. The state displays on the page, so your team can see whether a document is in progress, under review, or approved. States update as reviewers take action.

is a review action on a document. You assign one or more reviewers to a page. Those reviewers approve or reject the content at the appropriate stage in the workflow. The app records who approved, when, and at which stage.

monitors a specific event and performs an action in response. For example, you can configure a trigger to send an email when a document enters review, set an expiry date when content is approved, or restrict page editing during an approval stage.

is a configurable value within a workflow. Examples include a list of default reviewers, a review deadline, or a notification message. Parameters let you reuse the same workflow across spaces while adjusting values for each team or project.
Assign reviewers, set deadlines, and route pages through multi-stage approval workflows. Reviewers receive notifications when content needs their attention.
Every page with an active workflow displays its current state. Space administrators can view the status of all pages in a space using the document report.

Require reviewers to authenticate their decisions using e-signatures. Set expiry dates to flag content that needs periodic review. Use audit trails and reporting to support FDA 21 CFR Part 11, ISO 9001, and ISO 13485 requirements.

Set up email and on-screen notifications for specific workflow events. You can notify reviewers when they are assigned, alert authors when a document is approved, or flag content owners when a page expires.
Use page macros to show document state, approval status, and activity history directly on a Confluence page.
Integrate with Comala Publishing to separate draft and published versions of a page. You can configure workflows to publish content automatically when it reaches an approved state.

content.text: This article explains how compliance with sections 4.2.4 and 4.2.5 can be achieved when using Confluence with Comala Document Management. It also provides information about support for other standard elements and a list of the tools required for successful implementation.

Confluence is a wiki used to help teams collaborate and share knowledge efficiently. It acts as a document collaboration and repository, tracking what changed in each document, when, and by whom. Team members can create, share, and collaborate on content.
If your organization has an ISO-13485:2016 quality management system, you can leverage Confluence to meet many of the requirements of that standard.
Extending Confluence with Comala Document Management will help you meet the requirements related to the management and control of documents and records (sections 4.2.4 and 4.2.5).
Reviewing our complementary compliance statement for

Appfire does not claim compliance or certification of any of our tools, as it is impossible for any vendor to offer a compliant system. In addition to taking advantage of technical elements, compliant systems must implement the necessary procedural and administrative controls.
Need help setting up Confluence and Comala Document Management for controlled documents?
1. Checklist against the ISO 13485:2016 requirements of sections 4.2.4 and 4.2.5 (Control of documents, control of records)
Review and approve documents for adequacy prior to issue;

Comala Document Management provides a method of enforcing document review and approval processes. This approval process is supported by built-in electronic signatures and an audit log. The flexibility provided by the Comala Document Management macro language enables you to configure an approval process that reflects your defined documented approval processes and your different organizational roles.
Each Confluence page has a unique Space/Title combination.
Page versions are captured automatically, and comparisons between versions are provided.
Unique page identifiers can be allocated manually (i.e., using page properties or metadata).
Define the review and approval process that works best for you.
Review, update as necessary, and re-approve documents;
The approval process, as provided by Comala Document Management, supports the processing of updates according to the defined approval process.
Ensure that the current revision status and changes to documents are identified;

Comala Document Management provides the means to clearly distinguish between current and draft versions of documents. Some organizations go further and use Comala Publishing to help separate between approved pages and pages that are still in the authoring and approval process. It creates a structure of an authoring space, where approved documents are automatically published into an official space.
Confluence provides a complete history of changes to each document. If you set up a dedicated official space, this feature will show the difference between official versions of the page.
Ensure that relevant versions of applicable documents are available at points of use.
Users can access Confluence throughout the internet (per your network and security configuration) using any device.
Ensure that documents remain legible and readily identifiable;
Each Confluence page has a unique Space/Title combination.
Keeping your documents electronically ensures they are always legible.
External documents are identified, and their distribution is controlled
Confluence provides a way to attach external files to pages, providing the structure to align external documents with your internal structures (approvals, identification, access management)
Prevent deterioration or loss of documents;
Changes to documents are reviewed and approved by appropriate functions in the organization
The definition of the approval process in Comala Document Management supports a role-based approval and review process.
Documents are retained for a defined retention period
Confluence provides the mechanism to retain all pages, including their historical versions.
Records are a specific type of document,
Segregation and limited access to sensitive information.
Confluence provides facilities to limit access to documents in a granular manner.
Confluence also keeps historic versions of pages and provides comparisons between page versions.

It is required to review all your QMS documents periodically. Comala Document Management provides a built-in way to force documents to be re-approved after a set period (if they have not been reviewed during that time), hence ensuring no document is neglected in this review.

Confluence page templates are an excellent way to put all the forms in the hands of your team.

A Confluence page can be set up as the index of your MDF, with hyperlinks to all the relevant pages and files (either attachments or external links) included in your MDF. This provides an easy way to ensure that the MDF always points to the current versions of documents and prevents the duplication of information. The actual content that goes into the MDF can be, at the same time, easily retrievable to your use in a hierarchy and location that makes sense to them.

Confluence is a documentation tool used to help teams collaborate and share knowledge efficiently. It acts as a home for document collaboration and a repository, keeping track of what changed in each document, when, and by whom. Team members can create, share, and collaborate on content.

If your organization has an ISO-19001:2015 quality management system, you can leverage Confluence to meet many of its requirements. We believe that using Confluence across your organization aligns well with the standard's overarching objectives, such as improved communications, decentralization of quality processes, and knowledge sharing.
Extending Confluence with Comala Document Management will help you meet the requirements related to the management and control of documents (section 7.5, Documented information) .

content.text: If your team is using Confluence Cloud and has enabled the new Live Pages (Live Docs) feature, you may notice that Comala Document Management workflows are disabled while editing a Live Page. This article explains what this means, what is supported, and how to continue using Comala workflows alongside Live Pages.
What Happens When You Edit a Live Page?
When a Confluence Live Page is in edit mode, you will see the following message:
Interaction with Comala Document Management is disabled in edit mode."

attrs.alt: Comala Document Management with Confluence Live Pages enabled

content.text: Comala workflows (state transitions, approvals, etc.) are temporarily disabled.
You cannot interact with the workflow status or triggers while editing.
This limitation applies only during the Live Page edit session.
Does This Affect Workflow Data or History?
No. Comala Document Management continues to track the workflow history and state of the page. Once editing ends, workflow functionality resumes outside of edit mode.
If you want to use Comala workflows fully on a Live Page, follow these steps:
Step 1: Use the Live Page feature to take real-time notes or collaborate quickly.
Step 2: When you're ready to apply formal workflows (e.g., for review or approval), convert the Live Page to a regular Confluence page.
Step 3: Comala Document Management will now be fully functional on the converted page.
Can I Keep Using My Existing Pages?
Yes. Your existing Confluence pages (created before enabling Live Docs) are not affected. Comala Document Management works normally on those pages.
Is It Safe to Enable Live Pages?
Enabling Live Pages will not affect your existing workflow-enabled content. You can enable Live Docs across your site and continue using them alongside traditional pages.

pages.title: Use workflows to govern and manage your Confluence documents

content.text: Comala Document Management lets you automate the review and approval process for Confluence pages. By applying workflows at the space or page level, you ensure that critical documents are reviewed and approved by the right people, on time, thus reducing manual overhead and minimizing the risk of publishing unapproved content.
What are the ways teams benefit?
Route documents to the correct reviewers and approvers. Track and report all changes and approvals to meet regulatory standards and reduce the risk of non-compliance.

Give knowledge workers clear visibility into the documentation lifecycle. They can see which pages are approved, in progress, or need attention, which reduces the risk of outdated or incorrect information.
Automate lifecycle management to keep policies and procedures current. Set expiration dates that trigger review reminders to keep policies up to date, consistent, and secure.

Automated document lifecycle management ensures that only authorized users can review and approve documents. Workflows route content through a defined approval chain, so every document meets your organization's compliance requirements before publication.

Comala Document Management records all workflow activity, including who made changes, when they were made, and what was approved. This produces an accessible audit trail that supports regulatory requirements and helps demonstrate compliance to regulators and stakeholders.
Add an electronic signature layer with OTP (one-time password) e-signatures to protect content with encryption and authentication, safeguarding sensitive information during approvals.

When teams use Confluence as a knowledge base, readers need to trust the content they find. Workflows provide clear visibility into each page's lifecycle status, whether it is approved, in review, or needs attention.
This transparency improves documentation accuracy and reduces the risk of misinformation spreading through your organization. Authors know what needs work, and readers know what they can rely on.

Managing policies and procedures manually increases the risk of outdated processes, compliance violations, and inconsistent documentation. Workflows automate this lifecycle, so your team can keep policies up to date without manual tracking.
Set review intervals so you are notified when a policy is due for review and update.
Trigger notifications to reviewers when their attention is needed, keeping approvals on schedule.

Common questions about Comala Document Management for Cloud built on the Atlassian Forge platform.
Where are the workflow actions that used to appear in the page menu?

Workflow actions are no longer available from Confluence's three-dot page menu. All workflow actions, including approve, reject, assign, add/remove workflow, view activity, and update parameters, are accessed from the
Why doesn't the workflow state appear when I'm editing a page?
When a page is in edit mode or is a live doc, the byline does not display the workflow state. Workflow status is only shown for published pages in view mode.
Why does a previous page version show the current workflow state?
When viewing a historical page version, the workflow byline and Document State macro display the
workflow state, not the state at the time of that version. This is expected behavior in the current Cloud version and is not a data issue.
The Document Approval macro has partial historical-version awareness for approval activity rows.
Why isn't the workflow copied when I duplicate a page?

When a page is copied, the workflow state and page workflow assignment are not carried over. The workflow must be applied separately to the new page, either manually or via triggers (for example, label-based initialization).
Why can't I find my workflow where I expect it?
The Cloud version uses a different workflow scoping than the Data Center version. Here's where to look:

Why can I edit or delete the built-in workflow templates?
Built-in workflow templates (BAW, CEW, QMSW) can now be modified and deleted. This was not possible in the previous version and is intentional.
Deleting a built-in workflow may break space configurations that rely on it. Recovery may require engineering assistance.
Why can't I clear Document Activity records?

The "Clear Document Activity" feature has been permanently removed. Document activity records are retained for compliance and audit purposes. Records are only removed when the associated page or space is deleted.
Why can't I export or import workflow configurations?
Manual workflow configuration export/import (instance-level or space-level backup and restore of workflow definitions) is not supported in the current Cloud version.

Pages containing multiple Forge app macros may display some macros as blank. This is a known limitation of the Atlassian Forge platform affecting pages with multiple Forge macros. It is not specific to any single macro type.
Why does the workflow state briefly show incorrect information when navigating between pages?
